cim: Sources: Apollo's $40B chip financing for SpaceX is structured via a special-purpose vehicle, letting SpaceX keep it off balance sheet and rent the GPUs (Ellen DiMauro/Semafor)
cim_eredeti: Sources: Apollo's $40B chip financing for SpaceX is structured via a special-purpose vehicle, letting SpaceX keep it off balance sheet and rent the GPUs (Ellen DiMauro/Semafor)
szoveg_eredeti:
The colossal $40 billion financing that Apollo is lining up for SpaceX could hit markets as early as this week, but it won’t be hitting their balance sheet, according to people familiar with the matter.

The financing will go into an SPV, or special-purpose vehicle, allowing SpaceX to keep it off its own balance sheet and instead rent GPUs from its subsidiary. Apollo will be lending close to $20 billion of the deal upfront and then syndicating it or selling it to other investors later.

Other companies, including Meta, have utilized this kind of financial workarounds to keep debt off their bottom lines. It also allows the companies to keep their ratings elevated.

Portions of the seven-part deal could be sold to investors as early as this week. The arrangement includes an array of pricing — the bulk of which, $35.5 billion, will price at 8.3% and 7.75%, Semafor reported earlier.

Other, riskier parts of the deal will price even higher, at a blended rate that could exceed 9%, but will account for less than $3 billion of the overall financing.

Pricing for debt related to data centers and artificial intelligence has gotten more expensive for borrowers as investors get choosier about where they put their money and fret over the growing debt loads at companies in the AI buildout.

Apollo declined to comment. SpaceX didn’t respond to a request for comment.
